Q: Why does WordPress recommend using hooks instead of editing core files? A:

Just think what effort a simple update of your WordPress installation would be. You will need to remember where and what you edited in the core files. And then you need to apply your patches again on the new core files, sometimes at other places and in another way.

By using official hooks, you can simply update the installation, and you are good. It does not need any better reason.

If the contract of a hook changes, you will notice this in the release notes. Which you will read, of course. To adapt to such a change is most probably much simpler then to adapt to changes core files.

Q: @Transactional spring JPA .save() not necessary? A:

Within a transaction context, an update to a managed instance is reflected in the persistence storage at the commit/flush time, i.e., in your case at the end of methodB(). However, calling save() comes with a cost in scenarios like yours, as stated in Spring Boot Persistence Best Practices:

The presence or absence of save() doesn’t affect the number or type of queries, but it still has a performance penalty, because the save() method fires a MergeEvent behind the scenes, which will execute a bunch of Hibernate-specific internal operations that are useless in this case. So, in scenarios such as these, avoid the explicit call of the save() method.

Q: Parsing an XML column in T-SQL with a colon in the XML Structure A:

You are spot on about the colons. Those represent XML namespaces, and because your query doesn't define what diffgr: means, SQL Server doesn't know how to handle it. Also, your root <DataSet> has a default namespace (xmlns="google.com"), which complicates things further.

The quickest and easiest fix is to use the wildcard *: prefix. This tells SQL Server to ignore the specific namespace and just look for the tag name.

Also, in your original code, you were stopping at the Table node. Since you want the SessionID value (which is an integer), you need to go one level deeper.

Try this:

SELECT
    [XML_Data].[Result].value('(*:DataSet/*:diffgram/*:ExportDate/*:Table/*:SessionID)[1]', 'INT') as [SessionID]
FROM [dbo].[XML_Data]

By adding *: before every tag, you bypass all the namespace definitions (including the tricky ones that reset to empty strings like ExportDate). This should parse it correctly.
